newsitem.title: USA: ARCO, Anadarko join in Cook Inlet exploration.
newsitem.headline: ARCO, Anadarko join in Cook Inlet exploration.

text.p: Atlantic Richfield's Alaskan subsidiary and Andarko Petroleum Corp. have struck an agreement to combine their exploration efforts in part of Alaska's Cook Inlet, officials said.
The two-year alliance will cover 127,000 onshore and offshore acres of ARCO's upper Cook Inlet leasehold, the companies said last week. Financial terms were not revealed.
An ARCO Alaska spokesman said on Friday that Anadarko's seismic technology could prove fruitful in the Cook Inlet area, Alaska's oldest oil-producing region.
"Oil exploration really is about the application of new ideas, sometimes to old areas," ARCO Alaska spokesman Ronnie Chappell said. "New ideas and a fresh perspective can be very valuable."
The agreement does not include the Sunfish prospect, which was discovered by ARCO and partner Phillips Petroleum Co. or the Beluga River gas field.
Under the agreement, Houston-based Anadarko will manage an Anchorage-based exploration team made up of scientists from both companies, officials said.
Anadarko will serve as operator and earn a 50 percent share of ARCO's working interest in Cook Inlet leases by conducting new exploration work, officials said.
Chappell said ARCO will benefit from its expanded partnership with Anadarko, which has joined with Arco in explorign the North Slope's Colville River Delta area.
"We've been acting with them on the North Slope and we felt like it was a really good fit," he said.
Anadarko has had impressive exploration successes elsewhere, Chappell said.
An Anadarko official said that company will also benefit from the Cook Inlet partnership, which was effective Sept. 1.
"This agreement joins two companies with complementary strengths," John Seitz, Anadarko's senior vice president for exploration, said in a statement.
